title: Riak TS
text: Riak TS is a distributed NoSQL key/value store optimized for time series data. It provides a time series database solution that is extensible and scalable. Riak TS includes a complete build of Riak KV, but adds the ability to co-locate keys of the same series within the same quanta for fast and efficient READs.

title: Riak TS
text: It provides a time series database solution that is extensible and scalable. Riak TS includes a complete build of Riak KV, but adds the ability to co-locate keys of the same series within the same quanta for fast and efficient READs. As an available and partition-tolerant time series database, Riak TS uses a subset of SQL to make querying even easier.

title: Riak TS Release Notes
heading: Create Tables#
text: Riak TS enables you to define and configure tables of time series data as a riak bucket type, and write data to these tables. The schema of Riak TS’s tables are generated as bucket properties and installed as bucket types, which allows you to structure data as it is coming in and store both structured and semi-structured data.

heading: Limitations#
text: Column to column comparisons are not currently supported. Secondary indexing (2i) will not work with Riak TS. Riak search will not work with Riak TS. Queries are limited by the number of quanta they can span when specifying the time limits.

title: Querying Data in Riak TS
heading: Leap seconds and quantum boundaries#
text: Effectively, there is no way in the UNIX time scheme to differentiate an event that occurred during the extra second at the end of 1998 to something that occurred the first second of 1999. Similarly, Riak TS would treat `915148800` as the start of a new time quantum, and any data points which a client added for that second would be considered to be in the first time quantum in 1999. The data is not lost, but a query against 1998 time quanta will not produce those data points despite the fact that some of the events flagged as `915148800` technically occurred in 1998.

text: Now that you’ve planned and activated your Riak TS table, you are ready to write data to it.

title: Writing Data to Riak TS
heading: Writing Data#
text: Riak TS allows you to write multiple rows of data at a time. To demonstrate, we’ll use the example table from earlier: SQL

title: Writing Data to Riak TS

text: In the event that your write fails, you should: Do a binary search with half the data, then the other half, and etc. to pinpoint the problem; or Write the data one at a time until one fails.

title: Writing Data to Riak TS
heading: Writing Data#
text: You could also try the original write again. Failures may be transitory when servers are temporarily unable to talk to each other.

title: Writing Data to Riak TS
heading: Guidelines#
text: Batches should not be too large. In our testing, 100 rows per write is a sweet spot, but you should expect different results depending on your hardware and schema. Writes will assume that columns are in the same order they’ve been declared in the table. Timestamps should be in Unix epoch/UTC milliseconds.
